recaps.ending: In the ancient city, Jarvis takes one of the unusual objects being handled by the barrel-shaped creatures, provoking a mass attack. Tweel could escape alone but returns to help him, confirming that their alliance is more than temporary convenience. The two hold off the creatures and flee together. Near the human expedition, approaching rescue separates them: Jarvis is recovered by his companions while Tweel disappears back into the Martian landscape rather than joining the humans. Jarvis completes his account aboard the Ares and produces the object he carried away, giving the expedition tangible evidence that the city's mechanisms and inhabitants warrant further study. Yet his strongest conclusion is personal rather than material. Despite radical differences in body, language, and thought, Tweel repeatedly reasoned, cooperated, risked himself for another being, and behaved as a friend. The crew can return for the scientific discovery, but Jarvis does not know whether he will ever find Tweel again.
recaps.in_short: On the first human expedition to Mars, Jarvis crashes a survey rocket far from the ship Ares and begins a long walk back. He befriends Tweel, an intelligent birdlike Martian with whom he can share only a few words. Traveling together, they encounter forms of life that defeat familiar Earth categories: silicon creatures that build pyramids through their life cycle, a predator that traps victims with wish-shaped illusions, and barrel-like beings operating a vast mechanism in an ancient city. Tweel repeatedly recognizes danger and saves Jarvis. When Jarvis takes an object from the city's procession, the barrel creatures attack; Tweel chooses to stand with him rather than escape alone. Jarvis eventually rejoins the human crew with the object, while Tweel vanishes into the Martian distance. The sample promises an important discovery, but Jarvis regards his lost cross-species friendship as the greater find.

recaps.text: Aboard the first human ship on Mars, Jarvis tells Harrison, Leroy, and Putz how he survived after his survey rocket failed far from the Ares. Walking across the desert, he met Tweel, a fast-moving, birdlike Martian whose intelligence was clear even though their attempts at a shared language produced only a handful of meanings. Tweel accompanied him toward the expedition. Along the way they observed silicon-based creatures whose repetitive life cycle builds pyramid structures. They also entered the ruins of a much older city, where a hidden predator projected seductive illusions drawn from a victim's mind. Tweel recognized the trap and rescued Jarvis. Deeper in the ruins, crowds of barrel-shaped beings carried objects through a mysterious mechanical ritual. Jarvis took one of the objects for study and triggered an attack. Tweel returned to defend him when flight alone would have been easier, and the pair escaped together. As they neared the Ares, a human rescue craft approached and Tweel departed into the Martian landscape. Jarvis came back safely and retained the object from the city, offering his crewmates a concrete scientific prize from the journey. More important to him, Tweel's reasoning, loyalty, and willingness to risk himself showed that a being unlike any terrestrial animal could still be recognized as a person and a friend.

characters.description: The newly appointed ambassador from Lsel Station, a small independent mining habitat, sent to represent her home at the dazzling and dangerous heart of the vast Teixcalaanli Empire. A lifelong lover of Teixcalaanli poetry and culture, she is nonetheless an outsider determined to protect Lsel's independence. She arrives to find her predecessor dead and quickly realizes she has walked into a web of politics and murder she barely understands, with little support and less time.
characters.name: Mahit Dzmare

characters.description: A quick, elegant young Teixcalaanli official assigned as Mahit's cultural liaison, or asekreta, tasked with guiding the new ambassador through the customs, language, and etiquette of the City. Clever, ambitious, and genuinely curious, she becomes Mahit's closest ally and interpreter, helping her navigate a court where every phrase and gesture carries hidden meaning.
characters.name: Three Seagrass

characters.description: Mahit's predecessor as Lsel's ambassador to Teixcalaan, who served for many years and is found dead as the story begins. Charismatic and deeply enmeshed in imperial affairs, he left behind unfinished dealings and dangerous secrets. Lsel technology preserves a recorded imprint of his memories and personality, meant to guide his successor, making him a presence in Mahit's mind as well as a mystery she must solve.
characters.name: Yskandr Aghavn

characters.description: A powerful and self-possessed member of the Emperor's inner circle, close enough to the throne to shape events. Sharp, watchful, and hard to read, she takes an interest in Mahit's survival and offers a measure of protection, though her own aims in the unfolding crisis remain guarded. She is among the most formidable figures Mahit must learn to deal with.
characters.name: Nineteen Adze

characters.description: The aging Emperor of Teixcalaan, who has ruled long and now faces the pressing question of who will succeed him. Shrewd and weary, he had his own private dealings with Mahit's predecessor, and the shape of the succession he leaves behind hangs over the entire capital as ambitious figures maneuver for the throne.
characters.name: Six Direction

characters.description: A friend and fellow official of Three Seagrass, charming and a bit reckless, who is drawn into helping Mahit investigate the dangers surrounding her. His willingness to bend rules makes him useful and his connections handy as the intrigue deepens.
characters.name: Twelve Azalea

characters.description: A popular and ambitious military commander whose growing support among the soldiery and the crowds makes him a serious contender for imperial power. His rise threatens to tip the succession crisis into open conflict, putting him at odds with those trying to keep the transition orderly and the City at peace.
characters.name: One Lightning

recaps.ending: The succession crisis breaks into violence in the capital, but it is resolved not by the ambitious general One Lightning seizing the throne but by the old Emperor Six Direction giving up his own life in a public act designed to trigger an orderly succession and deny the coup its opening. In the aftermath, his trusted ally Nineteen Adze takes the throne as the new ruler of Teixcalaan. Mahit, having pieced together that her predecessor Yskandr had tried to trade Lsel's memory-implant technology for imperial protection, and that her own implant was sabotaged by a faction back home to stop exactly that, manages to preserve Lsel's independence. She refuses to surrender the station's secret technology to the Empire and keeps the most dangerous truths hidden. Loving Teixcalaanli culture yet fearing being consumed by it, she decides she cannot stay, and parts from Three Seagrass, whose bond with her has deepened, with the door left open between them. She turns toward home carrying the knowledge that something unknown and threatening is moving at the edge of Lsel's space, a danger that will shape what comes next.
recaps.in_short: Mahit Dzmare arrives at the capital of the Teixcalaanli Empire as the new ambassador from tiny, independent Lsel Station, only to find her predecessor Yskandr dead and her implanted memory-copy of him, meant to guide her, failing. Aided by her sharp liaison Three Seagrass, she investigates his death and uncovers that Yskandr had secretly bargained with the aging Emperor Six Direction, offering Lsel's prized memory-implant technology in exchange for the Empire's protection. As a succession crisis erupts and the ambitious general One Lightning moves toward a coup, Mahit realizes her own implant was deliberately sabotaged from home by a Lsel faction opposed to that bargain, and that Lsel's independence and its secret technology are the true stakes. To halt the coup and force an orderly succession, Emperor Six Direction sacrifices his own life, and his ally Nineteen Adze rises to the throne. Mahit secures Lsel's continued independence, refuses to hand over its technology, and, unwilling to be swallowed by the culture she loves, chooses to return home, while an unknown threat stirs at the edge of Lsel's space.

recaps.text: Mahit Dzmare travels from Lsel Station, a small independent habitat, to serve as its ambassador at the center of the immense Teixcalaanli Empire, a civilization whose language, poetry, and rituals she has admired all her life. On arrival she learns that her predecessor, Yskandr, is dead, apparently for some time, and that no one will give her a straight account of how he died. She is assigned a poised imperial liaison, Three Seagrass, to guide her through the City's customs. Complicating everything, the Lsel memory-implant that should carry Yskandr's experience and advice inside her head is not working as it should, leaving her almost alone in a place where a misjudged word can be fatal. She begins to suspect Yskandr was murdered and that she may be a target too.

Settling uneasily into the ambassador's residence, Mahit works with Three Seagrass to investigate Yskandr's death and finds that he was far more entangled in imperial politics than Lsel ever knew. The Empire is on edge over the looming question of who will succeed its aging Emperor, and factions are already maneuvering. Mahit gains a wary, powerful potential ally in the influential Nineteen Adze, but an attempt on her life makes plain how exposed she is. She realizes that the answers about Yskandr are bound up with dangerous secrets at the highest levels of the City, and that simply surviving will require her to understand a political game whose rules she is still learning.

Mahit uncovers that Yskandr had been conducting his own private negotiations with the Emperor Six Direction, dangling something Lsel guards very closely in exchange for the Empire's protection of the station. As she pieces this together, the succession crisis intensifies: the ambitious and popular military commander One Lightning gathers support that could carry him to the throne by force, and rival figures at court press their own claims. Unrest spreads through the City itself. Caught between loyalty to Lsel and her fascination with Teixcalaan, Mahit must decide whom she can trust while the stakes rise from her personal safety to the fate of nations.

The crisis tips toward open conflict as One Lightning's bid for power drives the City toward civil war, with violence reaching its streets. Mahit comes to understand that her malfunctioning memory-implant was not an accident but was deliberately sabotaged by a faction back on Lsel, one determined to stop Yskandr's bargain and keep the station's technology out of imperial hands. She grasps that Lsel's independence, and the secret of the very technology inside her own head, are the true prize being fought over. Working with Three Seagrass and her allies, she tries to steer events so that Lsel is not swallowed by the Empire nor destroyed in the chaos, even as the throne itself hangs in the balance.

To break the coup and force an orderly transfer of power, the old Emperor Six Direction takes his own life in a deliberate public act, denying One Lightning his path to the throne. In the settling of affairs, the formidable Nineteen Adze becomes the new ruler of Teixcalaan. Mahit, having exposed the tangled scheme around Yskandr's death and her sabotaged implant, secures Lsel's continued independence and refuses to hand over the station's memory-implant technology, keeping its most dangerous secrets safe. Though she loves Teixcalaanli culture and has grown close to Three Seagrass, she decides she cannot remain without losing herself to the Empire, and she chooses to return home. She leaves carrying the unsettling knowledge that an unknown threat is stirring at the far edge of Lsel's space, a shadow over whatever comes next.

characters.description: The Dragon Reborn, the champion who must confront the Dark One at the Last Battle. Calm, resolute, and quietly awesome in his power over the cleansed male One Power, missing his left hand, he has united many of the nations and now stands ready to lead the world into Tarmon Gai'don and to face the Shadow at Shayol Ghul itself.
characters.name: Rand al'Thor

characters.description: A ta'veren gambler and brilliant, reluctant battle commander from the Two Rivers, one-eyed after the price he paid rescuing Moiraine, carrying the memories of dead generals and a medallion that turns aside the One Power. Husband to the Seanchan Empress and holder of the Horn of Valere's fate, he is one of the few who can turn the tide of a battlefield by instinct.
characters.name: Mat Cauthon

characters.description: A blacksmith, wolfbrother, and battle lord from the Two Rivers, master of the world of dreams and able to speak with wolves. At peace at last with his gifts and his wife, Faile, at his side, he commands a great army and stands ready to guard the Dragon Reborn wherever the fight leads.
characters.name: Perrin Aybara

characters.description: The Amyrlin Seat of a reunited White Tower, young but formidable, having broken a usurper and the Black Ajah's grip on the sisters. She leads the Aes Sedai into the Last Battle and presses the nations to bind themselves to a lasting peace, wary of the Dragon Reborn's plan to break the seals on the Dark One's prison.
characters.name: Egwene al'Vere

characters.description: The Queen of Andor and Cairhien, an Aes Sedai, one of the women bound to Rand and carrying his children. Proud, capable, and determined to lead from the front, she takes a central role in commanding the united armies of the Light.
characters.name: Elayne Trakand

characters.description: The former Wisdom of Emond's Field, an Aes Sedai and the most gifted Healer of her age, wife to Lan. Fierce and stubborn, she is one of Rand's closest companions and means to stand beside him to the very end, whatever it demands of her.
characters.name: Nynaeve al'Meara

characters.description: The uncrowned king of Malkier and one of the deadliest swordsmen alive, bonded to his wife, Nynaeve. Having raised an army on his ride north, he holds the line at Tarwin's Gap against the Shadow's hordes pouring out of the Blight.
characters.name: Lan Mandragoran

characters.description: The Aes Sedai who first found the Dragon Reborn and set his path, believed dead for years until Mat rescued her from beyond the twisted Tower of Ghenjei. Weakened but wise and unbending, she returns to guide Rand and to help hold the fractious rulers to a common cause at the last.
characters.name: Moiraine Damodred

characters.description: A practical young woman who reads glimpses of the future in the auras she alone can see, and a keen scholar of prophecy. One of the three women who love Rand, she works to interpret the omens that may decide the Last Battle.
characters.name: Min Farshaw

characters.description: A full Wise One of the Aiel, once a warrior, proud and fiercely honest, a strong channeler. One of the three women tied to Rand by love and prophecy, she takes her place among the Aiel forces committed to the Last Battle.
characters.name: Aviendha

characters.description: Now Fortuona, Empress of the Seanchan, small, composed, and ruthless, wed by her people's custom to Mat Cauthon. Ruler of a vast empire whose armies collar channelers as weapons, she weighs whether and how to bring her power to bear against the Shadow.
characters.name: Tuon

characters.description: A legendary and formidable Aes Sedai, imperious and shrewd, long a difficult mentor to the Dragon Reborn. Respected and feared in equal measure, she remains close to the center of events as the Light marshals for the end.
characters.name: Cadsuane Melaidhrin

recaps.ending: A Memory of Light ends with the Shadow defeated and the world remade at terrible cost. The forces of the Light win Tarmon Gai'don, but many fall: Egwene al'Vere dies unleashing a power that turns the enemy's channelers against themselves; Gawyn Trakand, Siuan Sanche, and the great captain Gareth Bryne are among the dead; Lan Mandragoran slays the Forsaken Demandred in a duel and barely survives. The twisted peddler Padan Fain is killed by Mat. Perrin destroys the assassin Slayer and guards Rand in the world of dreams. At Shayol Ghul, Rand confronts the Dark One directly and chooses not to annihilate him, for a world stripped of the ability to choose evil would be a world of puppets; instead he seals the prison anew and closes the Bore. Bound soul to soul with his enemy Moridin, Rand walks out of the fighting in Moridin's healthy body while his own broken body is burned on a pyre. The world believes the Dragon dead, but he lives, anonymous and finally free, riding away alone. Min, Aviendha, and Elayne, who carries his children, keep his secret. The Wheel of Time turns onward into a new Age.
recaps.in_short: Tarmon Gai'don, the Last Battle, is fought at last. At the Field of Merrilor the nations bind themselves to the Dragon's Peace, and Rand goes to Shayol Ghul to face the Dark One while four great battlefronts hold the Shadow's armies of Trollocs, Sharans, and Forsaken. Lan holds Tarwin's Gap and, in single combat, kills the Forsaken general Demandred. Egwene falls destroying an army of Shadow channelers; Gawyn, Siuan, and the great captain Gareth Bryne are among the many dead. Mat, become the Light's supreme commander, turns the tide and the Horn of Valere is sounded to call the heroes of legend. In the Pit of Doom, aided by Nynaeve and Moiraine, Rand battles the Dark One in a contest of wills and visions, refusing to destroy him utterly because that would end humanity's freedom to choose, and instead reseals his prison. Rand's dying body is burned on a pyre, but his soul lives on in another man's body, and he slips away unknown, free at last, while Min, Aviendha, and Elayne, who carries his children, keep the secret. The Wheel turns, and a new Age begins.

recaps.text: Rand al'Thor of the Two Rivers was revealed as the Dragon Reborn, prophesied to fight the Dark One at the Last Battle and to break the world again. Guided out of hiding by the Aes Sedai Moiraine with his ta'veren friends Mat and Perrin, he claimed the sword Callandor, was accepted by the Aiel, conquered nations, killed several of the Forsaken, founded the Black Tower, and did the impossible by cleansing the male One Power of its taint, though he lost his left hand along the way. His friends rose with him: Perrin became a wolfbrother and battle lord and freed his wife, Faile; Mat, a peerless battle commander wed to the Seanchan heir Tuon, lost an eye rescuing the long-lost Moiraine from beyond the Tower of Ghenjei; Egwene broke a usurper to become Amyrlin of a reunited White Tower and shattered the Black Ajah's grip; Elayne won the thrones of Andor and Cairhien. After nearly falling to despair and madness, Rand was remade into a calm, certain man ready for the end. Now the seals on the Dark One's prison are breaking, Rand has declared he will shatter them and face the Dark One directly, and he has called the rulers of the world to the Field of Merrilor. Lan rides to hold Tarwin's Gap, and the nations gather for Tarmon Gai'don, the Last Battle.

characters.description: A thirteen-year-old boy living with his seriously ill mother. Conor is exhausted by a recurring nightmare he refuses to describe and angry at the pity and avoidance his mother's cancer has brought into his life. He tries to manage the household and school as if nothing is changing.
characters.name: Conor O'Malley

characters.description: A vast being that takes the shape of the old yew tree near Conor's home. It arrives shortly after midnight with immense strength and an expectation that Conor should fear it. Conor is less frightened of this visitor than of the nightmare that already wakes him.
characters.name: The Monster

characters.description: Conor's mother, who is undergoing treatment for cancer. She tries to reassure him and preserve their ordinary routines despite her weakness, while Conor clings to her confidence that the latest treatment will work.
characters.name: Conor's Mother

characters.description: Conor's maternal grandmother. Formal, blunt, and very different from Conor, she begins spending more time at the house as her daughter's illness worsens. Her talk of practical arrangements threatens the future Conor is trying not to imagine.
characters.name: Conor's Grandmother

characters.description: A schoolmate who was once Conor's closest friend. Lily told other pupils about his mother's illness, believing they should know, and Conor has not forgiven her for changing the way everyone treats him. She still tries to defend and reach him.
characters.name: Lily Andrews

characters.description: A quiet, controlled school bully who targets Conor with two companions. Harry understands that being ignored can hurt Conor more than open violence, and he uses the adults' reluctance to discipline a boy with an ill mother to deepen Conor's isolation.
characters.name: Harry

characters.description: One of Conor's teachers. Miss Kwan sees signs that he is being bullied and attempts to intervene, but her sympathy and careful handling also reinforce his sense that the adults around him no longer treat him normally.
characters.name: Miss Kwan

characters.description: Conor's father, who now lives in America with his second family. He returns for a short visit when Conor's mother deteriorates. Conor hopes his arrival offers a permanent escape, but his father has obligations and a life elsewhere.
characters.name: Conor's Father

recaps.ending: The monster forces Conor to enter the recurring nightmare in which his mother hangs above a dark drop and he loses his grip on her. Conor finally admits that part of him deliberately let go because he wanted the strain and uncertainty of her illness to end. He has mistaken that involuntary wish for a desire that she die and has been punishing himself for it. The monster tells him that thoughts can contradict one another and are not the same as actions. Conor's grandmother finds him beneath the yew tree and rushes him to the hospital. He reaches his mother's bedside shortly before her death. Supported by the monster, he can at last tell her that he does not want her to go while also releasing his hold when the moment comes. He and his grandmother face the loss together, their shared grief replacing some of their hostility. The monster's stories have not cured his mother; they have enabled Conor to speak the truth and survive it.
recaps.in_short: Thirteen-year-old Conor O'Malley is struggling with his mother's worsening cancer, bullying at school, and a recurring nightmare he cannot face. At 12:07 a giant being formed from the nearby yew tree begins visiting him. It promises three morally unsettling tales, after which Conor must tell a fourth story: the truth of his nightmare. The monster's tales challenge simple divisions between heroes and villains, while their violence spills into Conor's life. He wrecks his grandmother's sitting room and seriously injures his bully, yet adults respond with pity rather than punishment. When his mother's last treatment fails, Conor finally relives the nightmare and admits that, exhausted by fear, he once wanted the waiting to end and let her fall. The monster teaches him that the thought does not mean he wanted her dead. Conor reaches the hospital in time to tell his mother he does not want her to go, then lets her die without hiding from his love or grief.

recaps.text: Conor O'Malley wakes from the recurring nightmare he will not name, then hears his name called at 12:07. The old yew tree outside has become an enormous monster and approaches the house, but Conor reacts with more anger than fear. By morning the tree appears normal, though signs of its visit remain. Conor's mother is receiving cancer treatment and insists she will recover. At school, other pupils either pity or avoid him. His former friend Lily exposed his mother's illness to their classmates, and Conor has cut her off, while Harry and two other boys bully him. The monster returns and explains that it will tell Conor three stories. Afterward, Conor must tell a fourth: his own story and the truth concealed in his nightmare.

The monster tells its first tale, set in a kingdom where an apparently wicked queen is blamed after a prince's beloved dies. The prince claims that the queen murdered the young woman and rallies the people against her, but the monster reveals that the prince committed the killing and used the accusation to secure his throne. Even so, the monster protected him and helped drive away the queen, who was not a murderer but was no benevolent ruler either. Conor objects that the story offers no clear good person to support. The monster insists that people and their choices are rarely simple. The lesson frustrates Conor, who wants direct answers and, more urgently, wants the monster's healing power to save his mother.

Conor's grandmother arrives as his mother's condition worsens, and plans are made for Conor to stay at her immaculate house. His father visits from America but cannot offer the permanent new home Conor imagines. The monster's second tale concerns an apothecary who values the yew's healing power and a rigid parson who condemns him. When the parson's daughters become ill, he abandons his stated beliefs and begs the apothecary for help; the apothecary refuses because the man now believes in nothing. The monster then destroys the parson's home. Conor eagerly joins the destruction, only to find that he has in reality demolished his grandmother's sitting room. His grandmother is devastated, but she does not punish him in the conventional way he expects. The absence of consequences leaves him feeling even more cut off from ordinary life.

At school, Harry changes tactics and declares that he no longer sees Conor. This deliberate erasure breaks through Conor's restraint. The monster begins its third tale, about an invisible man who demanded to be seen, and Conor attacks Harry with the monster's force behind him. Harry is badly injured. Conor expects expulsion or severe punishment, but the headteacher treats him as a distressed child because of his mother's illness. Once again, exceptional sympathy makes him feel invisible rather than forgiven. Lily continues trying to reach him. Meanwhile, Conor discovers that his mother's new medicine is derived from yew trees and hopes this explains the monster's arrival. The treatment does not reverse her decline, and she is returned to the hospital. The monster refuses to promise a cure, forcing Conor closer to the truth he has avoided.

A note from Lily assures Conor that she still sees him, but his mother's condition is now critical. Conor runs to the yew tree and demands the help he thought the monster would provide. Instead, the fourth tale begins: Conor is placed inside his recurring nightmare, where his mother is falling into darkness and he is trying to hold her. He admits that he let go because the long ordeal had exhausted him and part of him wanted it to end. The monster explains that this thought does not mean he wanted his mother to die; conflicting feelings can both be true, and actions matter more than an unwanted thought. Conor's grandmother finds him and gets him to the hospital in time. At his mother's bedside, Conor finally says that he does not want her to die. When the end comes, he releases her while holding on to the truth of his love. His mother dies, and Conor faces the grief he had feared rather than remaining trapped by guilt and silence.

characters.description: The capable mistress of Little Paddocks. She supports an assorted household of relatives, friends, and lodgers, and responds calmly when a newspaper notice predicts a murder in her home.
characters.name: Letitia Blacklock

characters.description: Letitia Blacklock's affectionate, muddle-headed childhood friend. She lives at Little Paddocks and depends heavily on Letitia, whom she has known for many years.
characters.name: Dora Bunner

characters.description: A young man staying at Little Paddocks as one of Miss Blacklock's distant relations. Cheerful and theatrical, he treats the announced murder as entertainment until the shooting makes it real.
characters.name: Patrick Simmons

characters.description: A reserved young woman presented as Patrick's sister and another distant relation of Miss Blacklock. She is less open than Patrick about her reasons for being in Chipping Cleghorn.
characters.name: Julia Simmons

characters.description: A widowed mother lodging at Little Paddocks and working in a nearby garden. Quiet and self-contained, she is supporting her young son while his father is presumed lost in the war.
characters.name: Phillipa Haymes

characters.description: The volatile Central European cook at Little Paddocks. Traumatized by wartime persecution, she expects suspicion to fall on her and expresses every fear with dramatic intensity.
characters.name: Mitzi

characters.description: A young Swiss employee of a local hotel. He appears at Little Paddocks during the gathering prompted by the newspaper notice and enters the darkened room carrying a weapon.
characters.name: Rudi Scherz

characters.description: The county police officer leading the investigation. Methodical but imaginative, he takes Miss Marple's observations seriously as the case reaches into old identities and inheritances.
characters.name: Inspector Dermot Craddock

characters.description: An elderly visitor with a precise memory for social detail and a wide knowledge of ordinary dishonesty. She becomes involved through her acquaintance with the local vicar's wife.
characters.name: Miss Jane Marple

characters.description: A forthright farmer who lives nearby with Amy Murgatroyd. Her practical manner and close attention to the case make her an active participant rather than a passive village witness.
characters.name: Miss Hinchcliffe

characters.description: Miss Hinchcliffe's gentle companion. She was present during the shooting at Little Paddocks and later struggles to recover a crucial visual memory from the darkened room.
characters.name: Amy Murgatroyd

characters.description: A confident retired officer living in Chipping Cleghorn. He and his much younger wife attend the gathering at Little Paddocks after seeing the newspaper announcement.
characters.name: Colonel Easterbrook

characters.description: A local widow with a keen interest in village affairs. She and her son Edmund are among the neighbours who arrive at Little Paddocks expecting a party game.
characters.name: Mrs Swettenham

recaps.ending: Miss Marple and Inspector Craddock expose the woman called Letitia Blacklock as Charlotte Blacklock, Letitia's sister. The real Letitia died abroad, and Charlotte assumed her identity so that she could inherit when the elderly Belle Goedler died. Rudi Scherz recognized Charlotte from a Swiss clinic and became part of a staged robbery that she converted into his murder. Bunny's old memories and habit of calling her Lotty threatened the disguise, so Charlotte poisoned her; Amy Murgatroyd was killed after recalling that Miss Blacklock had not been in the room during the shooting. A trap using Mitzi and Miss Marple provokes Charlotte into attacking again, and she is arrested. Phillipa Haymes and Julia Simmons are revealed as the heirs Pip and Emma, and they inherit after Charlotte's scheme collapses.
recaps.in_short: A newspaper notice announces that a murder will occur at Letitia Blacklock's house. Curious neighbours gather; the lights fail, an armed man appears, and the intruder Rudi Scherz is shot dead. Further deaths show that the event concealed an old identity secret tied to an inheritance. Miss Marple discovers that the household's supposed Letitia is actually her sister Charlotte. The real Letitia died abroad, and Charlotte took her place to receive money due after Belle Goedler's death. Rudi recognized her, Bunny remembered too much, and Amy Murgatroyd recalled that she was absent during the staged shooting, so Charlotte killed all three. Miss Marple and Inspector Craddock trap her during another attempted attack. Charlotte is arrested, while Phillipa and Julia are identified as Pip and Emma, the alternative heirs.

recaps.text: The Chipping Cleghorn newspaper carries a notice stating that a murder will occur at Little Paddocks at 6:30 that evening. Letitia Blacklock denies placing it, but her neighbours arrive out of curiosity. Her household includes her old friend Bunny, the young relations Patrick and Julia Simmons, the lodger Phillipa Haymes, and the anxious cook Mitzi. At the appointed time the lights go out, a man shines a torch and orders everyone to raise their hands, and shots are fired. When the lights return, the intruder, hotel employee Rudi Scherz, is dead and Miss Blacklock has a wound to her ear. What looked like a prank or staged robbery has become a murder inquiry.

Inspector Craddock finds no simple explanation for the shooting. Rudi had a record of petty dishonesty and some contact with Miss Blacklock, but the room's layout, a recently oiled door, and the failure of the lights suggest advance preparation inside the house. Miss Marple joins the inquiry and studies the household's relationships. A large inheritance expected by Miss Blacklock depends on the death of the elderly Belle Goedler, while alternative heirs known only as Pip and Emma may be nearby under other names. Bunny's confused recollections of earlier years repeatedly unsettle Miss Blacklock, and small household incidents suggest that someone is increasingly afraid of what the old woman may remember.

Bunny dies after eating a poisoned birthday cake and taking medication from the wrong bedside table. Her death directs attention toward her habit of mixing past and present names. Meanwhile, Amy Murgatroyd works with Miss Hinchcliffe to reconstruct what she saw when the torch swept across the room. She realizes that one familiar person was not where everyone assumed during the blackout, but she is killed before she can report the name. Craddock investigates Miss Blacklock's life abroad and the history of her invalid sister Charlotte. Miss Marple concludes that the original shooting, the inheritance, and the household murders all depend on someone maintaining a false identity.

Miss Marple and Craddock reveal that the woman known as Letitia Blacklock is actually her sister Charlotte. Letitia died abroad, after which Charlotte assumed her identity to inherit Belle Goedler's fortune. Rudi Scherz had recognized Charlotte from a Swiss clinic; she arranged the supposed hold-up and shot him while using the darkness and a hidden route to preserve her role as victim. She later poisoned Bunny, whose memories exposed the name Lotty, and killed Amy Murgatroyd after Amy remembered her absence from the room. A staged confrontation involving Mitzi draws Charlotte into another attack, and she is caught trying to silence Miss Marple. Phillipa Haymes and Julia Simmons prove to be Pip and Emma, the alternative heirs, and Charlotte is arrested.

characters.description: A small, plump, unmemorable man, once an intelligence officer and now living quietly in Chelsea, no longer in government service. Scholarly, courteous and endlessly patient, he is a listener rather than an interrogator, and his talent is for noticing the detail that everyone else has smoothed over. He agrees to look into a reader's letter as a favour to a wartime colleague, and finds himself in a closed and self-satisfied world he understands well enough to see through.
characters.name: George Smiley

characters.description: The editor of a small nonconformist weekly with a devoted and elderly readership. Sensible, kind and conscientious, she worked in intelligence during the war, which is how she knows Smiley. A letter from a long-standing subscriber alarms her enough that she cannot simply file it, and she takes it to Smiley for advice.
characters.name: Ailsa Brimley

characters.description: The wife of a junior master at Carne, an ancient and expensive public school, and a faithful reader of the weekly to which she writes. Chapel-going, plainly dressed and known locally for her charity and good works, she is regarded by the school's wives as socially beneath them and by others as a modest, decent woman. Her letter states that her husband intends to kill her, and asks that nothing be done about it yet.
characters.name: Stella Rode

characters.description: A science master at Carne, the son of a small tradesman and a grammar-school and provincial university product, who has worked hard to acquire the manners of the place and is quietly despised for it. Anxious, punctilious and eager to belong, he is conscious at every moment of being an outsider among colleagues who were educated at schools like this one.
characters.name: Stanley Rode

characters.description: A detective inspector of the local county police handling the Carne case: solid, honest and shrewd, and well aware that investigating a great school means being managed by it at every turn. He knew Smiley's name from the war, welcomes his help, and shares his files with him more openly than his superiors would like.
characters.name: Rigby

characters.description: A senior housemaster at Carne, a large, theatrical and cultivated man in his last year before retirement, given to good wine, music and grand gestures, and to talking with practised indiscretion about the school he has served all his life. His brother served with Smiley during the war, which is the introduction that opens Carne's doors. Beneath the performance he is a disappointed man whose career never rose as far as he expected.
characters.name: Terence Fielding

characters.description: A master and the school's unofficial authority on precedence, dress and correct behaviour, fastidious to the point of absurdity and deeply invested in Carne's social hierarchy. He entertains carefully chosen guests, keeps house with his sister, and disapproves of the Rodes on grounds he would describe as taste.
characters.name: Felix D'Arcy

characters.description: D'Arcy's unmarried sister, who keeps house for him, breeds dogs and shares his views on who is and is not acceptable at Carne, expressed with rather less circumlocution than her brother uses.
characters.name: Dorothy D'Arcy

characters.description: The wife of one of the senior masters, a large, gracious woman who has spent decades in the school's society and reads it perfectly. Her conversation is elaborately polite and quietly destructive, and she dispenses gossip about her neighbours as a form of power. She is one of the few people at Carne who says anything about Stella Rode that is not simply admiring.
characters.name: Shane Hecht

characters.description: A vagrant woman, known locally as Mad Janie, who lives rough near the Rodes' house at the edge of the town and is treated by the town as a harmless lunatic. Stella Rode was kind to her, and she is found afterwards with belongings that were not hers. Her ramblings about what she saw that night are dismissed by almost everyone.
characters.name: Jane Lyn

characters.description: A boy in Fielding's house, amiable and not academically able, who is anxious about the examination results that will decide whether he can stay on at the school. He is grateful to his housemaster and reluctant to say anything that might reflect on him.
characters.name: Perkins

recaps.ending: Smiley establishes that Fielding had let the boy Perkins see an examination paper in advance so that he would not be removed from the school, and that Stella Rode obtained proof of it, along with knowledge of an earlier disgrace which Fielding had spent his career living down. Instead of exposing him she kept the evidence and let him understand that she had it, which was the private cruelty she practised on many people while the town admired her charity. With retirement and his reputation in front of him, Fielding killed her, and dressed the crime to point at her husband, whom Carne would have been happy to believe capable of it. When Perkins begins to talk about the examination paper, Fielding kills him too, in what is arranged to look like a road accident. Confronted with the reconstruction, Fielding admits what he did, and is arrested. Jane Lyn, who was the town's preferred culprit, is cleared. Stanley Rode is left innocent of the murder but with the truth about his marriage and no place at the school he tried so hard to enter. Smiley goes back to London with Ailsa Brimley, having exposed a killing that the school would rather have blamed on an outsider.
recaps.in_short: Ailsa Brimley, editor of a small nonconformist weekly, receives a letter from a reader, Stella Rode, saying that her husband intends to kill her, and takes it to her old wartime colleague George Smiley. Before anything can be done, Stella is beaten to death at her house on the edge of Carne, an ancient public school where her husband teaches science. Smiley goes down, is admitted to the school through the housemaster Terence Fielding, and works alongside Inspector Rigby. Carne assumes the murderer is either Stanley Rode, an outsider by birth and manner, or a local vagrant woman found with the dead woman's belongings; physical evidence has been arranged to incriminate the husband. Smiley finds that Stella's reputation for saintliness concealed a talent for collecting and using other people's shameful secrets. She had proof that Fielding had shown an examination paper to a boy in his house, and knowledge of an older disgrace that would have destroyed him. Fielding killed her to end it, staged the scene against Rode, and later killed the boy when he began to talk. Confronted, he confesses, and Smiley returns to London.

recaps.text: Ailsa Brimley edits a small nonconformist weekly with a loyal, mostly elderly readership. A letter arrives from Stella Rode, a long-standing subscriber and the daughter of a man the paper once honoured, saying plainly that her husband is planning to kill her, and asking that nothing be done for the moment. Uneasy, Ailsa takes it to George Smiley, with whom she worked in intelligence during the war and who is now retired and living quietly in London. Before they can decide how to respond, news comes that Stella Rode has been found beaten to death at North Fields, the house she shared with her husband on the edge of Carne, an ancient and expensive public school where he teaches science. The murder took place on a snowy night after a dinner at the house of Terence Fielding, a senior housemaster. Smiley travels down to Carne, where the county police, in the person of Inspector Rigby, are conducting an investigation hemmed in on all sides by the school's dislike of publicity.

Smiley is admitted to Carne society because Fielding's brother served with him in the war, and he begins to move between the school and the police station. Rigby shows him the case as it stands. Clothing belonging to Stanley Rode, along with other items, has been found in an outbuilding, footprints cross the snow, and the pattern of evidence points steadily at the husband. Rode himself is a nervous, meticulous man from a modest background who has laboured to be accepted at a school that will never accept him, and Carne's masters and their wives, among them the fastidious Felix D'Arcy and the formidably gracious Shane Hecht, make it clear that they regard him as a social intruder and would find his guilt unsurprising. The town, meanwhile, prefers a different culprit: Jane Lyn, a vagrant woman who lives near the house and has been found with belongings that had been Stella's. Smiley is struck by how conveniently the evidence has arranged itself and by how much everyone wishes to believe it.

Smiley begins to take apart the picture of the dead woman. Carne remembers Stella Rode as humble and charitable, active in her chapel, generous to the poor and to Jane Lyn in particular. What Smiley uncovers is a woman who studied the people around her for weaknesses and enjoyed possessing them: who humiliated her husband socially while appearing to support him, who told damaging stories in the guise of confidences, and who kept what she learned rather than using it openly. The letter she sent to the newspaper begins to look less like a frightened appeal than another move in a private campaign. At the same time Smiley picks at the physical evidence: the way the incriminating objects were placed, the timing of the walk home from Fielding's dinner and the movements of everyone who was at that table. The case against Rode is too complete, and the objects that convict him were left where they were certain to be found.

Attention narrows to Fielding, whose career at Carne is ending in disappointment and who is due to retire. Smiley learns that a boy in his house, Perkins, was in danger of being removed from the school after failing an examination, and that his paper was not what it should have been. Perkins is questioned and is frightened and evasive, unwilling to say anything against the housemaster who protected him. Shortly afterwards the boy is killed in what appears to be a road accident. Smiley concludes that Stella Rode had come by proof of what Fielding had done for the boy, and by knowledge of an older episode in his past that he had spent a lifetime burying, and that she had kept both without ever making a demand, so that he lived under her observation. The murder was Fielding's release from her, and the evidence in the outbuilding was placed to hang it on a husband nobody at Carne would defend.

Smiley sets his reconstruction in front of Fielding, who admits to killing Stella Rode and to killing Perkins when the boy began to talk, and he is arrested. Jane Lyn, whom the town had already convicted, is cleared. Stanley Rode is innocent of the murder, but the investigation has stripped away the marriage he defended: the wife everyone praised for her goodness had made a study of his shame, and he has no future at the school he tried to be worthy of. The masters and their wives close ranks around the school's reputation, less troubled by two deaths than by the noise. Smiley, who has no official standing and wanted none, leaves Carne with Ailsa Brimley and returns to London, having proved only that a closed community will believe any story that protects its own and blames an outsider.
